key_insight: An AI-based facial grading system closely matched expert ratings for several structural and lesion-related facial features, especially in more controlled image settings.
clinical_relevance: The approach could make dermatology assessments more scalable in hybrid and decentralized trials by enabling consistent smartphone-based image grading.
method: Compared AI grading with expert panel consensus across standardized studio, clinic smartphone, and home smartphone image settings.
Evaluated repeatability across independently captured images and agreement on multiple facial feature types.
Tested performance on macro-geometric, pigmentation, inflammatory, fine-texture, and color-dependent endpoints.
evidence_signal: Expert inter-rater reliability was good to excellent (median ICC 0.84–0.90), and the AI showed very high test-retest repeatability (median ICC 0.97–0.98) with strongest agreement for macro-geometric and some lesion features.
watch_item: Performance dropped for fine-texture features under less controlled acquisition, and color-dependent features remained limited across settings.
paper_title: Comparison of Facial Feature Grading by an AI-Based System Versus Human Expert Grading on Images Under Standardized Clinical and At-Home Settings
